name: Viscous gel-forming fibre
short: Trials of guar gum and glucomannan report abdominal pain, flatulence and diarrhoea or constipation. Reviews list guar gum and psyllium among reported causes of bezoars and of reduced drug absorption.
text: The cited evidence comes from individual gel-forming fibres rather than the class as a whole. In a meta-analysis of randomised trials of guar gum, the adverse events most frequently reported were abdominal pain, flatulence, diarrhoea and cramps, and 3% of patients dropped out because of adverse events; the authors concluded that guar gum is not efficacious for reducing body weight and that, considering these adverse events, its risks outweigh its benefits for that use; in a meta-analysis of glucomannan trials, adverse events included abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea and constipation. A review of bezoars formed from medicines (solid masses lodged in the gut) lists guar gum and psyllium preparations among the reported causes, attributes this to their water-absorbing properties, and notes that such masses most often occur in people with altered motility or anatomy of the gastrointestinal tract. A review of herb-drug interactions states that soluble fibres, including guar gum and psyllium, can decrease the absorption of drugs.
